title: How to Sell Feet Pics Anonymously: A Privacy Checklist for Beginners
excerpt: Worried someone you know will find out? This step-by-step checklist shows how to sell feet pics online without revealing your name, face, or location.
content:
The most common reason people never start selling feet pics is not the photography. It is the fear that a friend, relative, or colleague will recognise them. The good news is that staying anonymous is not complicated. It comes down to a handful of habits you set up once and then repeat every time you upload.

Work through the steps below in order. Most of them take only a few minutes.

Start with a separate seller identity

Before you create a profile anywhere, build an identity that has nothing to do with your real life.

  • Create a new email address that you use only for selling. Do not reuse an address that contains your name, birth year, or workplace.
  • Choose a username that reveals nothing. Avoid nicknames your friends use, your city, or a handle you already use on social media.
  • Keep the profile description general. You can describe what you offer without mentioning where you live, what you do for work, or where you study.

It is much easier to do this properly from the start than to untangle a personal account later.

Check every photo before you upload it

A photo of your feet can still say a lot about you. Look carefully at each image before it leaves your phone.

Look at what is behind you

Mirrors, windows, posters, doorways, letters left on a table, and distinctive furniture can all identify a home. A clean floor or a plain background removes the problem entirely.

Cover anything that identifies you

Tattoos, scars, birthmarks, and unusual jewellery are recognisable to people who know you. Decide in advance whether you are comfortable showing them, and frame or cover accordingly.

Switch off location tagging

Phone cameras can store the place a photo was taken inside the image file. Turn off location tagging in your camera settings before you shoot, so that information is never recorded in the first place.

You do not need to show your face

Most sellers never show their face, and a dedicated marketplace does not ask you to. Your profile does not need a face photo, a real name, or a location. If a buyer insists on seeing your face, you can simply decline. It is your content and your decision.

Keep every conversation on the platform

This is the habit that protects you most. When messages, payment, and delivery all happen in one place, you never have to share a phone number, a personal email address, or a payment app username.

Be cautious the moment someone asks to continue the conversation somewhere else. Moving to a private messaging app removes the protections the platform gives you, and it is where most problems begin. We cover the warning signs in detail in our guide to selling feet pics without getting scammed.

Let the platform handle payments

Paying a seller directly often exposes a real name on the receiving account. When the platform processes the payment and you withdraw your balance afterwards, buyers never see your banking or payment details.

Your anonymity checklist

  1. New email address used only for selling.
  2. Username with no link to your name, city, or other accounts.
  3. Location tagging switched off in your camera.
  4. Background checked in every photo.
  5. Identifying marks covered or cropped, if you prefer.
  6. No face, unless you have made a deliberate choice to include it.
  7. All messages and payments kept on the platform.

Anonymity is not one big decision. It is a short routine you repeat before every upload.

Once these habits are in place, you can concentrate on the part that actually earns money: taking good photos and replying to buyers. For more answers, see the frequently asked questions on our main guide.
